children: has fully financed its planned acquisition of Iridium Communications (NASDAQ:IRDM), removing one of the biggest uncertainties surrounding the transformative $8 billion deal while introducing a different consideration for shareholders: substantial equity dilution. The company raised roughly $1.94 billion by issuing 29.3 million shares and eliminated the need for a previously arranged $3.6 billion bridge loan.

Rocket Lab provides launch services through Electron while building satellites, spacecraft components and the larger Neutron rocket. Buying Iridium would push the company much further downstream, adding a global satellite communications network, spectrum rights and recurring service revenue to Rocket Lab's launch and manufacturing businesses.

Rocket Lab said proceeds from its completed at-the-market offering, combined with available liquidity and Iridium's existing financing, are sufficient to cover the required cash consideration and transaction expenses.

Iridium also amended its $1.775 billion term-loan facility to permit the change of control. That debt can now remain outstanding after closing, supported by Iridium's free cash flow and a Rocket Lab parent guarantee. Rocket Lab consequently terminated the $3.6 billion bridge facility, reducing refinancing risk ahead of the targeted mid-2027 closing.

The strategic prize is significant. Rocket Lab agreed in June to acquire Iridium for $54 per share in cash and stock. Iridium generated $871.7 million of 2025 revenue and $495 million of OEBITDA, providing Rocket Lab with a profitable recurring-revenue business alongside its more capital-intensive launch operations.
What Rocket Lab investors should watch next
Financing certainty strengthens the deal thesis, but investors now need to weigh dilution and execution.

The next major milestones are Iridium shareholder approval, remaining regulatory clearances including FCC consent, and progress toward the expected mid-2027 close. U.S. antitrust waiting periods have already expired.

If Rocket Lab successfully integrates Iridium, the acquisition could accelerate its transition into an end-to-end space company with recurring communications cash flow. But the issuance of 29.3 million new shares means management must ultimately create enough earnings and cash-flow growth to outweigh dilution, while integrating an $8 billion acquisition and simultaneously funding Neutron.

title: Rocket Lab Makes Bold Move to Broaden Space Business
